zones.label: Column 1 running header
zones.note: Lexical coverage was cross-checked after independent scan reading against the supplied NINJAL, Hideyuki Ohshima and Taichi Aida, Entry Words Data of Nippojisho, version 202510 (CC BY 4.0). The scan, not the lexical index, determines this transcription’s spelling, typeface, and lineation.

lines.note: Quaran is calamity and disorder, explained by Vazauai midare. The scan supports u in Vazauai, not OCR n, and the preceding page's catchword anticipates this entry.
Completes the definition with disturbance and upheavals accompanying the troubles. The Portuguese reuoltas retains the printed u/v spelling.

runs.text: Adu Modo de abrir aporta de

lines.note: Quararito describes opening or spreading something wide. Adu has no secure following stop in the scan; the Portuguese clause continues below.

runs.text: par em par, ou de estender totalmente algũa

lines.note: Opening a door wide and spreading something completely are parallel illustrations of the adverb. The printed joined aporta above and algũa here remain.
Couſa, &c. closes the spreading-something definition. The next physical row starts a distinct Quarei entry that the provisional OCR omitted.
The omitted Quarei entry is restored from the scan. Qeccôni bibixiqi coto explains splendour or fine appearance; Couſa begins the Portuguese gloss completed below.
Describes the thing as very beautiful, splendid, and grand. This continuation belongs to the restored Quarei row, not to Quararito.
Quareina is the adjectival form with the same sense. Quareina detachi illustrates a splendid appearance or outfit; italic Vt, replaces the OCR's false paragraph sign.
The example means clean, splendid clothing or attire. A genuine paragraph sign introduces another example beginning with the divided Qua-.
Reina completes Quareina; furumai is a feast or entertainment, translated as a splendid banquet. It is a second example of the same adjective.
Quareini is listed separately as the adverbial form of the splendour adjective. No Portuguese words are printed on this indented row.
Quareiſa is the corresponding quality noun, with visible long ſ. Like Quareini, it is listed without a fresh Portuguese definition.
Quareô is a penalty for an offence, explicitly Togano quatai. The eô sequence is retained; im- begins the divided Portuguese verb.

runs.text: poem por algũa culpa, ou delicto. Vt,

lines.note: Poem completes impoem, a penalty imposed for a fault or offence. The example begins Qua-, the first part of Quareôuo.
Reôuo daſu completes the example of paying a penalty. Pagar atal pena retains the printed joining of a and tal.
Quari, explained by Fanano vchi, means inside a flower. The Portuguese offers rose or flower, with the final alternative below.
Flor completes the alternative to rose; the vowel is o, not OCR e. The upright S. labels written usage.
This second Quari means inside the fire, explicitly Fino vchi. Its written-register S. is upright, and the entry is distinct from the flower sense.

runs.text: Hum certo pao da China hum pouco

lines.note: Quarin names a Chinese wood described as somewhat red. The gloss does not by itself settle a modern botanical identification.
Vermelho completes the colour qualification of the Chinese wood. The short continuation is part of Quarin, not the next sound-symbolic entry.

runs.text: Adu. Modo de ſoar a cou-

lines.note: Quariquarito describes the sound of chewing something hard. The example substance and remaining Portuguese clause follow on the next row.

runs.text: ſa dura como caramelo quando ſe maſtiga.

lines.note: Completes the chewing-sound comparison with something hard, called caramelo. The historical word is retained without imposing a modern confectionery interpretation.
Quariǔ is explained by Fana and yanagui, flower and willow. The caron belongs to the final u; the Portuguese salgueiro is divided after ſal-.
Gueiro completes salgueiro, willow. The upright S. marks this flower-and-willow expression as written usage.

runs.text: Males cauſados do fogo, ou queima.

lines.note: Quaſai denotes harm caused by fire or burning. The gloss specifies a fire disaster rather than the mere presence of fire.
Quaſan, Fanano yama, is a mountain of flowers. The Portuguese flores is divided after flo without an added hyphen.

runs.text: res, ou onde eſtà florecido o mato.

lines.note: Res completes flores; the alternative describes a mountain where the vegetation is in blossom. The older eſtà and florecido remain.

runs.text: O queimar o corpo do defunto dando

lines.note: Quasǒ denotes burning a deceased person's body as a form of burial. The printed short s and final caron are retained.

runs.text: lhe desta maneira ſepultura, ou fazendolhe o

lines.note: The explanation treats cremation as giving burial or performing the funeral. Fazendolhe remains joined as printed.
Enterramento completes the burial explanation. Quasǒ ſuru is the example for cremating; the extra i in OCR Qiuasǒ is absent from the scan.
Completes Queimar with a dead body treated in this way. It closes the cremation example before the house-of-fire entry.
Quatacu, Fino iye, is literally a house of fire. The Portuguese explicitly identifies the metaphor with this world on the next row.
Mundo completes Este mundo, the gloss for the metaphorical burning house. No additional religious explanation is inserted into the canonical text.

runs.text: Caſtigo, ou pena que ſe dà por algum

lines.note: Quatai denotes a punishment or penalty imposed for an offence. The definition prepares the example of imposing such a penalty.
Quataiuo caquru means imposing a penalty. The visible final Portuguese word is Impor, not OCR Impos; its object follows below.

runs.text: pena por algum crime. ¶ Item, Pecado,

lines.note: Pena por algum crime completes imposing a penalty for a crime. Item then introduces the separate sense of a sin or fault.
Ou falta closes the second sense, a fault. It is an indented continuation, not a new headword.
Quatdat denotes largeness, magnificence, or generosity. The abbreviated Grãdeza keeps its printed tilde; the list continues with liberalidade.
Liberalidade completes the generosity sense. Quatdatni fodocoſu illustrates bestowing something in a generous manner.
Dar liberal, & magnificamente translates the giving example. Chi- begins a new example about understanding or knowledge, not a Portuguese word.
Ye completes Chiye, understanding. Quatdat nari describes it as broad and clear; the entire Portuguese Tem is italic, correcting the OCR's isolated roman T.
Saber completes the preceding description of broad, clear understanding. Quatdatna chiye supplies the adjectival version of the same idea; claro is divided after cla-.

runs.text: ro, & grande, & que ſe estende a todo genero

lines.note: Ro completes claro. The explanation adds that this extensive understanding reaches every kind of thing, with the object completed below.
De couſa closes the universal-scope explanation of understanding. This short row finishes Quatdat before the next headword.
Quatei, Fanano ſoco, denotes the middle or interior of a flower. Meo and dẽtro preserve the Portuguese forms actually printed.

runs.text: Quatei.. Fino ſoco. i, Fino vchi.

lines.note: This Quatei is instead Fino ſoco, further explained by Fino vchi, inside the fire. The repeated stop after the headword is retained as printed.
Do fogo completes Dentro do fogo. It is the final body continuation in the first column, above the rule.
Quatet is heated or incandescent iron, explained by Fino curogane. Abraſado is the printed Portuguese form; no modern spelling is substituted.
Quatmiacu is identified as a particular pulse. The short gloss does not specify its diagnostic characteristics, so none are supplied in the transcription.
Quatnin is a person returned to life, explicitly Yomigayeru fito. The Portuguese reſuſcitado is divided after reſuſ-.
Citado completes reſuſcitado, resurrected. This short continuation belongs to the person entry, not the following expression of thanks.
Quatǒ is an expression of gratitude or appreciation, equated with Quabunna coto. The headword includes t, omitted by OCR, and the Portuguese agradecimento begins after de.
Gradecimento completes agradecimento. The explanatory formula expresses holding something in high esteem; Go- begins the Japanese letter-of-thanks example.
Jǒ completes Gojǒ, the other person's letter. Quatǒno itari expresses extreme appreciation, translated with many thanks for the letter.
Ta completes carta, the letter sent by the addressee. The upright S. marks the written-language formula.

runs.text: Hũa maneira de touca, ou veo que ſe

lines.note: Quatô, with circumflex rather than the preceding caron, denotes a cap or veil. The artificial OCR space after Q is removed.

runs.text: amarra na cabeça por de baixo da barba.

lines.note: The head covering is tied beneath the beard. De baixo remains two printed words rather than modernized debaixo.
Quatocu is recompense in the other world. The upright Bup. identifies a Buddhist term; its stop belongs to the same roman label.
Quatto describes giving generously or opening something wide. The initial sense is followed by a spreading-out sense on the next row.

runs.text: ou de abrir, & eſtender algũa couſa totalmẽte.

lines.note: Completes the adverb's opening and spreading sense: something is extended completely. Algũa and totalmẽte retain their abbreviation tildes.
Quauǒ is explained by the repeated Vazauai, calamities or troubles. The Portuguese trabalhos is divided after tra-.
Completes tra-/balhos in the preceding definition: the first Quauǒ entry concerns calamities and afflictions, not the flower named in the next entry.
A second Quauǒ is equated with Botan and described as a certain large rose-like flower; the separate entry and caron distinguish the printed form without conflating its sense with calamity.
Completes the flower description with “and beautiful”; the very short continuation belongs to the Botan entry.
Fanano iye explains Quauocu as a house associated with flowers; the Portuguese begins a description of a house built in a particular setting.
Completes the setting with many fulas and roses. The scan reads fulas, an unexpected form in this floral context; it is retained rather than silently replaced by flores. The terminal S. is upright.
Fino curuma corresponds directly to a chariot of fire. This is a separate Quaxa homograph; the terminal S. is upright.

runs.text: Homem que ſe trata bem, & luzida-

lines.note: The next Quaxa describes a man who maintains an elegant appearance; the adverb luzida-/mente continues onto the following line.
Completes the description of elegance in clothing and related matters, rather than the preceding fire-chariot sense.
A third Quaxa, explained by Fanaguruma, is a richly ornamented carriage. The Portuguese adjective is divided or-/nado across the line boundary.
Completes or-/nado, “ornamented,” and closes the carriage entry with an upright S.
Xacuuo caquru explains Quaxacu through a lodging practice. The Portuguese begins the account of a monk taking accommodation; the following line supplies the subject Bonzo.
The monk takes lodging in a house by placing a book inside. Bonzo is visibly upright amid the italic Portuguese; the nasal mark in algũa is retained.

runs.text: ou outra peça em ſinal q̃ toma aquella pouſada.

lines.note: Completes the lodging practice: a book or another object signals that the monk is taking that lodging. The printed q̃ abbreviation is preserved.
Fanano yeda explains this Quaxi as a branch bearing roses or flowers; it is distinct from the fruit and verbal entries below.
Supplies flores as the alternative to roses, completing the preceding branch definition.

runs.text: Fruita: propriamente ſe diz da frui-

lines.note: The second Quaxi means fruit, especially fruit served at the end of a meal. Its final frui- continues on the next physical line.
Completes frui-/ta and specifies de ſobre meſa, dessert fruit; the historical spacing is retained.
The verbal Quaxi has the listed forms ſuru and ita and means to soften. A paragraph sign introduces the example beginning Fito-, continued below.
Continues Fito-/no cocorouo qua ſuru, an example about softening someone’s heart; the Portuguese translation likewise continues after cora-.
Completes cora-/ção dalguem, “someone’s heart,” and closes the example with upright S.
Fino fari explains Quaxin as a fire-heated needle or iron point; the Portuguese agulha is divided a-/gulha.
Completes the needle description as heated in fire and starts the example Quaxinuo; the roman example is separate from the italic definition.

runs.text: Meter eſte ferro abraſado no corpo.

lines.note: Completes the example with tatçuru and translates it as putting the heated iron into the body. This is the source’s historical description, not a modern treatment recommendation.
Quaxit is glossed as a fault or error; the short entry ends here and is not the beginning of the next phrase.
Quaxita fito describes a liberal or generous, grand-mannered man; the phrase is a separate lexical item from Quaxit.

runs.text: Carta, ou patente que ſe dà a hum pe-

lines.note: Quaxo is a letter or authorization issued to a person, with its purpose continuing after pe-.

runs.text: ra o deixarem paßar por algum certo lugar,

lines.note: Completes pe-/ra and explains that the document permits passage through a certain place. The right-edge punctuation is a comma, not the draft’s full stop.
Adds “or passage/checkpoint,” completing the explanation of the travel authorization.
Fino xǒ explains Quaxǒ as the nature of fire. Both long-vowel signs are downward-pointing carons in the scan; they are not changed to circumflexes.
Fanauo cazaru explains Quaxocu in terms of ornament or lustre. This is an independent entry, followed by its adjectival form.
Quaxocuna describes something lustrous and well ornamented; the original short-s spelling in lustroſa is retained.
Restores the clearly printed paragraph sign before the example. Quaxocuna fito applies the quality to a man whose manner of dress is described on the next line.
Completes the description as dressing cleanly and splendidly; the upright S. closes the entry above the separate signature and catchword.

zones.label: Column 2 catchword
zones.note: Catchword anticipates the beginning of Quaxocu on the next page.
